questions.q: What real workaround had the finance team been using for three years, per this lab's scenario?
options: The table had been deleted and rebuilt as a spreadsheet from the start
Analysts had been given the finance_admin role directly with no restrictions at all
No workaround existed; analysts simply did without the data
A weekly full export of every field in expense_line_item, including the approval-chain override field, emailed to a twelve-person analyst team with no ACLs or audit trail
questions.explain: The blanket field-level lockdown pushed the team toward a weekly unaudited export -- exactly the shadow-export pattern from Lesson 16.

questions.q: In Step 1, what distinguishes the approval-chain-override field from the other four fields on the table?
options: It's the only field with no access restriction at all
All five fields carry exactly the same level of risk
It's the field analysts use most often in their daily work
It's the only field that is both not needed by analysts daily and genuinely sensitive, since it records who bypassed a control and why
questions.explain: The other four fields are needed daily and carry no special risk; only the override field justifies continued tight restriction.

questions.q: What does the redesigned finance_analyst role actually grant, and why does that matter?
options: Full finance_admin access to every field, including the override field
Access to the override field only, with the other four fields still locked

Read access to exactly the four fields analysts need daily, with the override field's existing finance_admin-only ACL left unchanged -- removing the reason to export without loosening the genuinely sensitive field
No access to any field, forcing the export workaround to continue
questions.explain: This is Lesson 16's judgment applied concretely: frictionless where risk doesn't justify restriction, strict where it does.

questions.q: Why isn't fixing the ACL alone considered a finished recommendation in Step 3?
options: ACL changes in ServiceNow automatically disable any related scheduled jobs
Fixing the ACL alone is sufficient and no further verification is needed
Analysts cannot be notified of a role change under any circumstances
The scheduled export job and the habit of requesting exports have to be deliberately retired and then verified, or the workaround can quietly continue even after the role exists
questions.explain: Shipping the new role isn't the same as confirming analysts stopped relying on the export -- that follow-up check is what proves the fix actually worked.

questions.q: If a new ad hoc export request appears a few weeks after the fix ships, what should the architect conclude?
options: Some analyst likely needs a field the finance_analyst role doesn't currently cover, and the role definition should be revisited
The entire expense_line_item table should be deleted
The fix was already a complete success and the request should be ignored
The override field should immediately be opened up to all analysts
questions.explain: A recurring export request after the redesign is a direct signal the role's field coverage is still missing something analysts legitimately need.
